resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy for Change in Occupancy (certificate of continued occupancy)
resale_co.issued_by: Lower Alloways Creek Township Housing and Zoning Officer (Zoning Housing Office)
resale_co.lead_time: Schedule the inspection at least 10 business days before settlement. The inspection is only scheduled after the completed application and the required certifications are received.
requirements: Buyer must get the certificate before buying and moving in; the home may not be occupied until it is issued
Well water test by a New Jersey state approved lab
Fire extinguisher mounted on the wall no higher than 5 feet, within 10 feet of the kitchen, not blocked
GFCI outlets in the kitchen, bathrooms, sump pumps, utility sinks and outside
Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors must be new 10-year sealed battery units
Water heater discharge pipe ending 2 to 6 inches from the floor
Electrical panel with every breaker labeled
Yard free of debris, trash and junk; grass and weeds mowed
Owner or owner's representative must be present if the home is vacant
resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Township's Application for Certificate of Occupancy for Change in Occupancy and gather the septic, well water, chimney and other certifications. The application is not complete until the owner or realtor contacts the Housing/Zoning Officer (856-935-1549 x 6560 or zoning@lowerallowayscreek-nj.gov) to schedule. Bring a $50.00 check payable to Lower Alloways Creek Twp to the inspection.

APPLICATION IS NOT COMPLETE UNTIL THE OWNER/REALTOR CONTACTS THE HOUSING/ZONING OFFICER TO SCHEDULE THE APPOINTMENT. PLEASE CALL 856-935-1549 X # 6560 or EMAIL zoning@lowerallowayscreek-nj.gov THIS DWELLING IS NOT TO BE OCCUPIED UNTIL A CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY IS ISSUED BY THE HOUSING/ZONING OFFICER OF LOWER ALLOWAYS CREEK TOWNSHIP.

resale_co.notes: The live Township website (www.lowerallowayscreek-nj.gov) shows a Cloudflare bot check and was not opened; all Township pages and files here are Internet Archive copies of the original URLs https://www.lowerallowayscreek-nj.gov/zoning (captured 2026-04-02), .../sites/g/files/vyhlif3381/f/uploads/co_application_2023.pdf and .../lac_co_pre_inspection_list09242024_0.pdf (captured 2025-02-16), and .../lac_code_ver01012020.pdf (captured 2024-07-02). The zoning page hides its email address with Cloudflare email protection; it decodes to zoning@lowerallowayscreek-nj.gov, which also appears in plain text on the application. The 2020 code book (section 99-7 D) says to apply at least 10 days before sale and sets the fee at $25 for the first and second inspections and $50 for each later one, but the Township's zoning page says the fee became $50.00 for inspections as of March 21, 2023, which matches the current application; the newer $50 figures are used. The archived home page (2026-08-31) and search results say the Township is taking applications for a Zoning Officer (due September 30, 2026), so the named officer may change. Zoning office hours in the April 2026 capture were Tuesdays 4:00 pm to 5:30 pm April through September and Saturdays October through April. The pre-inspection list still requires a fire extinguisher; P.L.2025, c.19 (February 3, 2025) removed it from the state smoke certificate rule, but it remains on this Township list (dated 09/24/2024).

requirements: Township certificate of occupancy list requires new 10-year sealed battery smoke and carbon monoxide detectors

authorities.how_to_apply: Unconfirmed. The Township certificate of occupancy inspection checks smoke and carbon monoxide detectors; ask the Housing/Zoning Officer whether it also issues the state smoke and carbon monoxide certificate or whether to apply to the NJ DCA.

evidence.quote: SMOKE/CO2 DETECTORS (must be the new 10-year battery sealed units)

authorities.name: NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (State is the fire code enforcing agency)
authorities.how_to_apply: Do not rely on the State's online smoke certificate application for this town: the DCA portal data marks LOWER ALLOWAYS CREEK TWP-001 as smoke-certificate exempt, which means the town is not offered in the State's online application. Ask the Township who issues the certificate; the DCA Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement can confirm.

fire_cert.notes: Who issues the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate here is not settled. The State (NJ DCA) is the fire code enforcing agency (registry code S; state directory code 1704), and the directory lists 'NJ Division of Fire Safety' under smoke detector compliance. But the DCA's state towns list (revised 7/17/2026) shows Lower Alloways Creek without the 'SC' (State issues smoke certs) mark, and the DCA portal marks LOWER ALLOWAYS CREEK TWP-001 as smoke-certificate exempt, which in other towns has meant the municipality issues the certificate itself. The Township's certificate of occupancy inspection checks the detectors, but no Township page says it issues the state certificate. The 2020 Township code (section 92-2, Ord. 2009-18) named the Lower Alloways Creek Township Fire District's Bureau of Fire Prevention as the local enforcing agency; the July 2026 state registry now lists the State instead, so that bureau is not treated as current. No fees are recorded until the issuer is confirmed. The Lower Alloways Creek Fire company (Chief Don Hinchman Jr.) is the volunteer fire company, not an inspecting agency. The DCA's online smoke application loads its town list from the same portal data feed; towns marked smoke-certificate exempt, as this one is, are not offered there, so the State's online route should not be given to agents for this town.

other_items.label: Septic certification, well water test and chimney certification
other_items.detail: Must be received before the Township will schedule the certificate of occupancy inspection; the well water test must be done by a New Jersey state approved lab.
